title: New Apple Hardware Rebuild Runbook
remarks: Turnkey steps to rebuild ExoMac (Mission Control host) onto new Apple hardware, e.g. the Mac on order. The asset backup is the DATA layer; this runbook covers the full-machine restore and the reconnect steps Migration Assistant does not self-document.
objective: restore a fully working Mission Control host onto new Apple hardware with minimal downtime, covering the OS, runtime stack, integrations, data, and automation, then verify.
overview: The asset backup (mc.db + CRM + MC data + automation fleet + config) is the granular, verifiable DATA layer. It is NOT a full-machine image. The whole-machine restore path to new Apple hardware is Time Machine + Migration Assistant (Path A). A clean install (Path B) uses the captured system-manifest (Brewfile, pip freeze, versions) to reproduce the runtime stack. Either path finishes with reconnecting integrations, restoring/verifying MC+ERP data, and a smoke test.

tasks.name: 0 - Before you start (verify + gather)
steps: VERIFY Time Machine is current: System Settings > Time Machine, confirm the last backup is recent. A stale TM = a stale restore.
Gather: the Time Machine drive, the encrypted off-site archive from SharePoint IT backups + its passphrase (from the password manager), the Git repo URL, and admin credentials.
Confirm the new Mac is Apple Silicon (clean Apple-Silicon to Apple-Silicon migration).

tasks.name: Path A - Migration Assistant from Time Machine (fastest, recommended)
steps: Power on the new Mac; at Setup Assistant choose 'From a Mac, Time Machine backup, or startup disk'.
Select the Time Machine drive and the latest backup; migrate Applications, User account (exomac), and system files.
This restores macOS user data, /opt/homebrew and the runtime stack, ~/.openclaw, /Library LaunchDaemons, and the workspace. Proceed to 'Reconnect integrations'.

tasks.name: Path B - Clean install (only if not using Migration Assistant)
steps: Install macOS; create the 'exomac' account (and the admin account).
Install Homebrew, then reproduce the stack:  brew bundle --file system-manifest/Brewfile  (node, python, mise, ollama, cloudflared, gpg, msmtp, etc.).
Restore Python libs:  pip install -r system-manifest/pip-freeze.txt  (into the PYTHONPATH used by the crons).
Install OpenClaw (npm) and restore ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json + secrets.json + .env from the backup.
Clone the workspace repo and  git checkout  the commit in the snapshot manifest (git_head).

tasks.name: Reconnect integrations (after either path)
steps: Proton Bridge: install and log in; confirm local IMAP 1143 / SMTP works (email tracker + sends).
Cloudflare One client: re-enroll ExoMac to the exosaero Zero Trust org (so MC is reachable and RDP/VPN works).
Verify keychain items migrated; re-auth Ollama models if missing (ollama pull as needed).
Confirm ~/.msmtprc and ~/.protonmail-bridge.crt are present.

tasks.name: Restore + verify MC / ERP data
steps: Restore local-only data from the latest verified asset snapshot: erp-foundation/mc.db, mission-control/data, uploads, process-library, capture, config, users.json, .ds-passcode.
Verify integrity:  python3 scripts/mc-asset-backup.py --verify <snapshot>  (expect 0 mismatches).
If Supabase was also lost, re-import supabase-export/*.json (tasks, activities, contacts, companies, deals).

tasks.name: Bring services up + smoke test
steps: Load the automation fleet: the 69 com.exos.*.plist LaunchAgents (launchctl bootstrap) and the root com.exos.mission-control LaunchDaemon.
Start Mission Control; open http://<MC-LAN-IP>:8080 and check the board, an upload, a CMMC 2.0 doc, and one integration (e.g. an email send).
Confirm the nightly backup runs and targets the attached drive.

tasks.name: Post-restore
steps: If a compromise was suspected, rotate credentials (Supabase keys, DocuSign passcode, integration secrets) before returning to service.
Run one manual backup to confirm the new host is protected.
Record the actual recovery time (RTO) and fold any gaps back into PLAN-DR.
